novelty_flags.label: ass:strong-tier-monotonicity; related_work; project_justification
novelty_flags.one_line: Kroft--Mourifié--Vayalinkal is mischaracterized as precedent for ordered-layer strong monotonicity: its Assumption 2 is only binary positive-selection monotonicity, and its multilayer response types explicitly permit both L→H and H→L transitions.

soundness_flags.label: ass:strong-tier-monotonicity
soundness_flags.one_line: The condition P(D1≥D0)=1 is not the standard condition supported by the cited Kroft--Mourifié--Vayalinkal reference; retag it as novel protocol monotonicity and retain its independent design justification.

accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The diagonal box, prism, and harm interval are sharp conditional on an enforcing protocol that prohibits tier downgrades.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv:2409.04589v2, revised 5 February 2025; cited revised-manuscript version
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Assumption 2 is P[1{D1>0}≥1{D0>0}|X]=1, whereas the response-type system retains arbitrary positive-layer transitions; it does not impose D1≥D0. Theorem 1(iii) is instead a sharp aggregate-LCDE result optimized over the response-type set.
Theorem 2 gives a sharp interval for the fraction negatively affected from observed treatment-arm outcome marginals, with sharpness established by Fréchet--Hoeffding coupling.

The paper concerns ordered categories of the outcome, gives sharp tiered-benefit bounds with and without its outcome monotonicity condition, and reports tiered-harm analysis; this differs from protocol-assigned selection tiers.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Replace every assertion that Kroft--Mourifié--Vayalinkal supplies ordered-tier monotonicity with an accurate comparison: their Assumption 2 prevents exit from positive selection but allows reciprocal positive-tier movement; retag the proposed order restriction as novel protocol monotonicity.
Add a formal boundary theorem showing exactly how the prism collapses to the published binary-selection/probability-of-causation interval when L=1, rather than leaving that comparison only in prose.

Sharpen practical relevance with a second nondegenerate protocol design or an explicit sensitivity result allowing a bounded amount of downward tier movement, thereby showing what empirical violation of the maintained order restriction does to the harm interval.

recommended_next_step: Correct the Kroft--Mourifié--Vayalinkal comparison and retag the ordered-tier condition as a novel, protocol-justified maintained restriction; then continue to Stage 0 on the conditional field-tier identification kernel.
